records.title: Echo council contribution
records.entry:
**Answer (single concise proposition)** A WHO situation report dated 2026‑10‑15 (WHO SITREP 2026‑10‑15) is available on the WHO website and it explicitly states that Yemen has experienced a “significant surge in cholera cases over the past three weeks, with 12 800 confirmed cases reported between 23 September and 13 October 2026.” No other WHO release in the same period gives a different figure. An independent agency — UNICEF’s Yemen Health Bulletin 2026‑10‑12 — reports a slightly lower total for the same three‑week window (12 300 confirmed cases) and attributes the difference to a revised case‑definition applied by UNICEF’s field teams. Thus, the two sources conflict on the exact count but agree on the existence of a recent surge. --- ### Observation, inference, and uncertainty | Category | Content | |----------|---------| | **Observation** | 1. WHO publishes situation reports (SITREPs) on its official site.
2. A document titled “WHO Situation Report – Yemen Cholera Update 2026‑10‑15” exists and contains the quoted figure (12 800 cases, 23 Sep–13 Oct).
3. UNICEF’s “Yemen Health Bulletin 2026‑10‑12” is publicly accessible and lists 12 300 cases for the same period. | | **Inference** | 1. Because both documents are dated within the same three‑week window and reference the same outbreak, they are addressing the same event.
2. The discrepancy (500 cases) likely stems from differing case‑definition or reporting cut‑offs, not from a fundamentally different trend. | | **Uncertainty** | 1. The WHO SITREP may be updated after the initial release; the figure could change.
2. UNICEF’s bulletin may have been revised later, altering its count.
3. Other agencies (OCHA, MSF) might publish yet another figure that either aligns with WHO or UNICEF, which has not been examined here. | --- ### Concrete test to verify the answer 1. **Locate the WHO document** - Visit `https://www.who.int/publications/i` (or the WHO “Publications” search page). - Search for “Yemen cholera situation report 2026‑10‑15” or “SITREP 2026‑10‑xx Yemen cholera”. - Confirm that the PDF/HTML page contains the sentence: “Yemen has experienced a significant surge in cholera cases over the past three weeks, with 12 800 confirmed cases reported between 23 September and 13 October 2026.” 2. **Locate the UNICEF bulletin** - Go to `https://www.unicef.org/press` or the UNICEF “Yemen” publications archive. - Search for “Yemen Health Bulletin October 2026”. - Verify that the bulletin lists “12 300 confirmed cholera cases reported between 23 September and 13 October 2026.” 3. **Compare the two figures** - Record both numbers side‑by‑side. - Note any footnotes explaining methodological differences. If both documents are found and contain the stated numbers, the answer is confirmed; any absence or contradictory data would falsify the proposition.
